title: Dissent from U.S. Policy Toward East Pakistan (The Blood Telegram)
publisher_or_archive: Foreign Relations of the United States (FRUS), 1969–1976, Volume XI, South Asia Crisis, 1971 / US Department of State
summary: Historic diplomatic cable sent on April 6, 1971, by US Consul General Archer Blood and 20 staff members formally protesting US complicity in the Pakistani military crackdown in East Pakistan: 'Our government has failed to denounce the suppression of democracy. Our government has failed to denounce atrocities... We, as professional civil servants, express our dissent with current policy and register our belief that our government has made a grievous error.'
